name: Craterhorn
body:
Craterhorn
CR 12

Before you stands what seems to be an enormous bull made entirely of jagged, volcanic stone. Its tail is long and covered in spikes, and its head is devoid of any features, except for a pair of monstrous, beetle-like mandibles.

XP 19,200
N Huge magical beast
Init +1; Senses blindsight 120 ft., tremorsense 300 ft.; Perception +23;

DEFENSE

AC 27, touch 9, flat-footed 26 (+1 Dex, +18 natural, –2 size)
hp 195 (17d10+102)
Fort +16, Ref +11, Will +10
DR 5/—; Immune bleed, cold, disease, electricity, fire, paralysis, poison; SR 23
Weaknesses blind, vulnerable to sonic

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee bite +25 (3d8+9/19-20), 2 hooves +23 (1d8+4), tail slap +25 (3d6+9/19-20)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 15 ft.
Special Attacks spiked tail, trample (3d8+13, DC 27)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 17th; concentration +18)

At will—gravel vortex
3/day—gravity well (DC 16), reverse gravity
1/day—air walk, cosmic ray (DC 17)

STATISTICS

Str 29, Dex 12, Con 22, Int 3, Wis 16, Cha 13
Base Atk +17; CMB +28; CMD 39 (43 vs. trip)
Feats Diehard, Endurance, Improved Critical (bite, tail slap), Iron Will, Multiattack, Weapon Focus (bite, hoof, tail slap)
Skills Perception +23
SQ gravity mastery, no breath

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Blind (Ex)

A craterhorn sees and senses exclusively through its blindsight and tremorsense abilities. Beyond their range, it is considered blind. A craterhorn is immune to all sight-based effects and attacks, including gaze attacks.

Gravity Mastery (Su)

A craterhorn never takes penalties from its gravity effects and can always choose to be affected or unaffected by any gravity effects it is targeted by or in area of.

Spiked Tail (Ex)

A craterhorn’s tail spikes allow the creature’s tail slap to deal both bludgeoning and piercing damage. A craterhorn’s tail slap is a primary attack.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, pair, or colony (3-8)
Treasure incidental

Craterhorns are curious creatures that bear many traits common to earth elementals, which is why they are most often mistaken for a subtype of those beings. The truth is perhaps more bizarre, as while craterhorns lack any extraplanar origins, they instead come from the vastness of space. Craterhorns seem to be composed entirely of dark stone, though their insides bear mineralized structures similar to organs found in most living beings. They have an unusual lifecycle, which is strongly tied to their means of reproduction and spreading to other habitats. A young craterhorn lands on a planet just like a meteorite would, crashing through the atmosphere and into the ground. It then starts its new life, alone, having all the skills needed for survival. It seeks out a mineral-rich territory, often in rocky areas, to have a suitable supply of food. While not territorial creatures and not prone to searching out interlopers, craterhorns are aggressive to most beings that don’t immediately make themselves scarce upon encountering them. Craterhorns feed on rocks, with a strong preference for volcanic rock, especially of denser and harder variety. They feed by “inhaling” the rocks using a localized gravity vortex and then merging them with their bodies in a poorly understood way. Craterhorns are often picky and search diligently for good enough stone to integrate and those specimens surviving on subpar diets not only seem to have their growth stunted, but appear sickly and weak in general. A craterhorn that reaches a large enough size begins to seek out its kin, most often those that fell onto the planet in the similar timeframe it did. Larger craterhorns in the newly formed colony then help the smaller ones to feed and grow, until the group is powerful enough to proceed to the next stage. This stage sees the colony gather tightly into a ball and proceed to use their control over gravity to lift themselves off the ground, and in time – off the planet. It is believed that those creatures then travel through space on a randomly set course, in time merging into a single organism, which then periodically breaks off pieces of itself much smaller than the original members, which are the new and numerous young craterhorns. Those pieces are launched away from the cluster and onto the planets to start the cycle anew. It is unknown if the craterhorns have any way of understanding if the celestial body in the vicinity is abundant in needed minerals or even habitable.

Craterhorns are named for the craters that they leave upon impact and in which they sometimes then live. The second part of their name is misguided, as it comes from their mandibles which were mistaken for a set of horns by the first people to saw them. Due to their way of reproduction, craterhorns are entirely genderless and asexual.

A fully grown craterhorn is 25 feet long and weighs 30 tons, although some specimens grow even larger if no colony gathers. Young craterhorns are typically large sized and have 12 HD. They lack the air walk and cosmic ray spell-like abilities and their gravity well and reverse gravity spell-like abilities are usable once per day. This heavyset creature hops awkwardly on four legs, its skin warty and toadlike. Droplets fall off its trumpet-like mouth, and you see them hiss and burn through the ground.
